body:
## Why

Observed 2026-09-22 on the Budget tab:
- Two unrelated money panels one above the other: "Trip cost" (4 components) and "Budget vs actual" (9 categories: lodging, transport, food, activities, local mobility, fees, contingency, workspace, client hospitality). A traveller cannot tell which one the packet uses.
- "Budget vs actual" shows `$0.00` everywhere and **"Remaining -$0.00"**, with developer copy "Planned caps, actual spend drift, and remaining category headroom should feed later planner tradeoff reasoning and in-trip replans" (`frontend/src/components/budget/WorkspaceBudgetPanel.tsx:261`).
- The Trip cost panel renders in Title Case ("No Source Has Priced This Yet.") because it reuses `.focus-area-list`, whose `li` has `text-transform: capitalize` (`frontend/src/styles.css:729`). The same rule produces "Transfer(S)" in Compare.
- All four save buttons are named "Save" (no per-component accessible name).
- "Other costs" can only reach "0 of 4 unpriced" if the traveller knows to type 0; nothing says so.

## Tasks
- [ ] Put "Budget vs actual" behind a disclosure labelled for after-trip use, or remove it until caps come from policy (see TPP issue on budget caps); never render `-$0.00`.
- [ ] Give TripPricesPanel its own list class; remove `text-transform: capitalize` from `.focus-area-list li` or scope it to tag chips.
- [ ] `aria-label="Save <component>"` on each save button; add "Enter 0 if there are none" to "Other costs".

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Test gate** `TripPricesPanel.test.tsx` asserts each save button has a distinct accessible name; `WorkspaceBudgetPanel` test asserts no `-$0` text. **Deliberate break:** revert the aria-labels — gate fails; revert passes.
title: Budget tab: two competing money panels, -$0.00, and Title Case price labels
